title: Lock Call Bonus: Thanksgiving Drama on the Bricks
blurb: The gang hosts Thanksgiving at The Window. The boss explains the whole operation, cannot stop looking at Mateo, and somebody barges in before dessert.
kind: bonus: an AI clone of Matthew's voice plays the boss at the table (eleven_multilingual_v2), with Mateo and Tiff joining the cast; the real Matthew's own recording is the last-scene barge-in; not made by the daily render

lines.text: [alarmed] Brett. The boss came to our Thanksgiving, and he will not stop staring at Mateo.
[grinning] One turkey, two bombshells, and a whole lot of stuffing talk. Go!
From The Window at Hardwood Bricks, this is the Lock Call Thanksgiving Extravaganza! I'm Brett Busberger.
And I'm Leslie Phyllis. The whole gang is at one table tonight. Merv is carving. And Edwin brought a guest.
[wheezing] This is Dutch. He don't talk. Don't ask.
[dry] He is sitting in my chair, Edwin.
And we have company from upstairs. The boss, Matthew. And from the U C Irvine desk, Tiffany Park.
[stunned] Wow. Tiffany. That dress should come with a point spread.
[purring] It does, Brett. And I always cover. Barely.
And from New Mexico... oh my. Mateo Sandoval.
[warm] Good evening, everyone. I came straight from the gym. I hope the singlet is okay.
[low] Lord. Even I looked.
[breathless] It's more than okay. Mateo, sit by me. I insist. I have wanted to get behind you all season. Professionally.
[flirty] Matthew, there's a seat right here. On me. I mean, next to me.
[polite] No thank you, Tiffany. I'm all set.
[solemn] Lord, bless this food. And the under. Amen.
[gruff] Before I eat. Somebody tell me what this joint actually is. Who's paying for the bird?
[proud] Happy to, Edwin. Hardwood Bricks dot com is mid-major college basketball, every single night. Twenty-seven conferences. Every school gets its own anchor.
[pointed] Two hundred eighty-six of us. He named every one. Matthew, ask me what I'm wearing under this apron.
[polite] Layers, I hope. It's November. Second course. This room is The Window. Tops and Bottoms. Four handicappers, eight picks a night, every unit kept.
[grumbling] Tops and Bottoms. He named that too.
[innocent] I did! I love both. I'm flexible. Mateo, which do you prefer?
[carefully] ...The over, boss.
Third course. The films, the weekly papers, and Mateo's sleep videos.
[dignified] I record rain for eight hours. People fall asleep to my window.
[dreamy] I have watched all eight hours. I never fall asleep.
[curious] So who makes all of this?
Me. And some help.
[dry] Young man. We are the help.
[whispering] And now... As the Brick Turns.
[sincere] Mateo, would you grab the rolls? Low oven. Take your time. Really bend into it. For your back.
[flat] That is three trips for rolls. We have rolls.
[calm] Brett. Status.
[calm] Under control. I hid the rolls. Merv has the knife. Dutch is watching the door.
[dry] We run a sportsbook, Leslie. I have seen worse by halftime.
[earnest] Merv, you're rushing that bird. You can't just jam the stuffing in. You warm it up. You go slow. You ask how the bird is doing.
[slow] I have never once asked the bird.
[breathy] Matthew. My car broke down. My hotel is full. And I get so cold at night.
[concerned] Oh no. Brett, can the machine find her a blanket?
The machine says there's a ninety-four percent chance she is not asking for a blanket.
[musing] You know my favorite play in basketball, Mateo? The back door. Nobody sees it coming. It's tight, it's quick, and when it's done right, everybody goes home happy.
[wheezing] Even I caught that one, and I've been asleep since the yams.
[quietly] He is talking about basketball. I am almost sure he is talking about basketball.
And what is this envelope at Mateo's plate? [gasps] That's a JuiceBox Nation logo!
[quickly] I have never seen that envelope in my life.
[bright] A toast! One thing you're thankful for. Leslie?
Second place. For now.
[deep] Nine, four and one.
[swelling] I am thankful for our president. Tremendous man. The best. Nobody ever pardoned a turkey like him. They say he could carve this whole bird with one hand...
[sharp] Not now, Edwin.
[firm] Especially not now.
[muttering] Dutch agrees with me.
[flat] I'm thankful I wore this for absolutely no one.
The independent media clause in my contract.

[heartfelt] I'm thankful for this team. For commitment. For shoulders. For a sequin singlet in November. Mateo, my back office is always open to you. Or yours. Whichever. I am happy to come in through the rear.
[low] Leslie. Does he know?
Mateo?
The boss.
[sighs] I am flattered. I think. I would like to finish my yams.
Oops. Dropped my fork. Mateo, would you?
[calm] Boss. It's your fork.
Hey, what the hell's going on in here?
[gasps] Matthew?!
[nervous] ...Yes?
[slow] Young man. There are two of you.
[urgent] Which one signs the checks?
[deadpan] Two of them. And neither one is looking at me.
[weary] Two bosses. One fork. I am going home.
[dramatic] Which boss is the real boss? What is in the envelope? And who is Dutch? Find out... never.
[warm] Picks are back tomorrow morning at hardwood bricks dot com. Happy Thanksgiving, everybody.
Twenty-one and up. If gambling's a problem, call one eight hundred GAMBLER.
Keep it mid. Keep it real.

notes.site_facts: 27 conferences and 286 schools per the front page on Nov 26; Tiff's '286 of us' left as is on Matthew's call (Watch page says 284 anchors).
notes.fiction: Every character and plot point is fictional comedy. Dutch, the envelope and the two bosses are invented.
